## Natural history notes

A medium-sized erebid moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown wings with dark wavy lines and a leaf-litter-like pattern that helps it blend against bark and dead leaves. In Florida, the Maple Looper Moth is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, forest edges, parks, and wooded yards where maples and other hardwood host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars are looping inchworm-like feeders on tree foliage, helping move hardwood leaf growth into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
